text:
maya: Quick alert — after the latest kernel-weight rollout we're seeing a host-side p95 uptick for small-chat requests. Started ~09:12 UTC on canary.

samir: Confirmed on canary. P95 +95ms for short sequences (10-120 tokens). Flame points to parse/tokenize + many small writev syscalls.

maya: Sample flame: parse_request -> tokenize (utf8-normalize) -> kv_lookup -> grpc_writev. KV hit-rate dipped from 88% -> 80% on the shard.

alicia: Likely chunk boundary shift from kernel hint change. Splitting cached prefixes is my bet. We can try a simple prefix-preserve (keep trailing 6 tokens as one key) behind a flag.

jon: Also seeing HTTP2 lots of 200-400B frames. HPACK and syscall overhead add up. Current ingress coalesce = 200us. Could increase to 600us for small traffic.

ryan: Ran a local microbench: coalesce 200->600us => writev count down ~2.7x, parse CPU down ~7-9% for small reqs. End-to-end p95 delta ~60-80ms.

samir: Plan:
- revert kernel-weight on single shard
- deploy coalesce=600us behind flag to canary shard
- prototype prefix-preserve N=8
- run batch-bias sweep to nudge minibatches toward 8-12 for small-seq workloads

maya: I pushed a canary PR for coalesce flag: https://git.internal/r/redwood/ingress/pulls/4342

ci-bot: Build passed. Canary plan set for shard s-42.

ryan: Canary up (s-42) with coalesce=600us + kernel-weight reverted. Early metrics (5m): p95 down ~55ms vs bad canary, KV hit-rate ~83%, writev down ~2.4x.

alicia: Draft PR for prefix-preserve: https://git.internal/r/redwood/ingress/pulls/4344. Added unit tests and microbench.

jon: Samir, please run batch-bias runs and post flame graphs. If selector made tiny minibatches more likely, biasing toward slightly larger minibatches should amortize host overhead.

samir: On it. Quick config I'm testing:
{"workload":"small-chat","batch_bias":1.25,"minibatch_target":10}

maya: Actions: samir run batch-bias (ETA 2h), alicia finish prefix-preserve (ETA 3h), maya monitor canary (30-60m), ryan standby rollback.

ci-bot: Metrics snapshot: https://metrics.internal/redwood/canary/6501234567

maya: Early conclusion: root cause = host-side small-write churn + KV fragmentation. Coalesce + kernel revert help immediately; batching and cache heuristics next. Will reconvene after samir's sweep. :thumbsup:
